introduction: The Qur’an’s verse of light, a lamp in a glass in a niche, “light upon light”, stands at the head of this guide, and the readings unfold its parts: light as what makes all things visible, the heart as wick, believers as mirrors or as candlesticks of different shapes for one flame, and colour as what light becomes in different glasses. Then come the colour-vocabulary of the Báb’s writings and a few remarks on colours and feeling. Light is the most universal of religious images, and the companions come from everywhere: “Let there be light”; “God is light”; the lamp not hidden; Plato’s sun, which makes things visible as the good makes them knowable; Aristotle’s mind like light; Rumi’s lamps; Dante’s glory shining more in one part and less in another; Milton’s “Hail, holy Light”. Shelley’s dome of many-coloured glass says in a line what reading 13 says of white and the colours. Keats is the one objector: he feared that to analyse the rainbow is to unweave it.
questions: The verse of light has a niche, a glass, a lamp and oil. How does reading 4 assign these, and what would change if the assignments were different?
Rumi says the lamps differ and the light is one; reading 6 says the same of candlesticks. What does the image allow one to say about the differences among believers, or among religions?

Reading 13 argues from the composition of white light that black and white have no importance. Keats thought such analysis destroys the rainbow. Can a scientific fact carry a symbolic meaning without loss?
The readings end with “be thou as a candle”. How does the symbolism of light become a description of conduct?

outside.why: The reading interprets this verse: God is the Light of the heavens and the earth; the similitude of His light is as a niche wherein is a lamp; the lamp is in a glass; the glass is as it were a shining star; light upon light.
“Light is the manifestor of all things.” It is the first thing called for: let there be light.
Plato made the same observation the hinge of his philosophy: the sun is the author of visibility in all visible things, and in like manner the good is the author of knowledge to all things known.
Light shining through glass illumines what is around it. No man, when he hath lighted a candle, putteth it in a secret place, but on a candlestick, that they which come in may see the light.
The wick is the heart; the oil, knowledge; the light, love. The spirit of man is the candle of the Lord, searching all the inward parts.
Those who follow what they hear are as light from the light of God. God is light, and in him is no darkness at all; if we walk in the light, we have fellowship one with another.
Truth is one light; the candlesticks vary. Rumi: the lamps are different, but the Light is the same.
Some bodies have their own light and some borrow it. Dante opens his Paradiso: the glory of Him who moveth everything doth penetrate the universe, and shine in one part more and in another less.
There are three kinds of light, and the highest is that of the intellect. Aristotle compares mind itself to light: for in a sense light makes potential colours into actual colours.
The light of the eye, which sees what the sun only shows. The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.
A black stone gives back nothing; a pure mirror reveals the sun. We all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image.
Paul also knows a mirror that is not clear: for now we see through a glass, darkly. What polishes a mirror, on the readings’ account?
The station of light is the station of the Word. In him was life; and the life was the light of men.
A lamp of utterance has been lit in the niche of creation. The light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
White garments signify a station “sanctified from color”. On the mountain his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light.
White conceals seven colours, so whiteness and blackness have no importance. Shelley: life, like a dome of many-coloured glass, stains the white radiance of eternity.

The reading draws a moral from the physics of light. Keats feared what that physics does to wonder: philosophy will clip an angel’s wings, conquer all mysteries by rule and line, unweave a rainbow. Does the knowledge that white contains the colours add to the symbol or take from it?
A school’s vocabulary of colours for stages of the divine action. Emerson’s general principle: every natural fact is a symbol of some spiritual fact.
A spring that clothes the world in rose and hyacinth and violet. The Song: lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone; the flowers appear on the earth.
“Be thou as a candle among the friends.” Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works.
A prayer for light from God’s nearness. Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights.
The mysteries of love depend on spiritual senses, not worldly ones. Blake: if the doors of perception were cleansed every thing would appear to man as it is, infinite.
Green “brings tranquility and joy to the heart”. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul.
Mirrors of different colours give back the one sun differently. Hopkins: glory be to God for dappled things; he fathers-forth whose beauty is past change.
A litany of leaves, white, yellow, green and red. The first colours given a meaning in the Bible are the rainbow’s: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant.
East and West became “the vale of Sinai”. The bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
Milton, blind, begins a book of his poem by greeting what he cannot see: hail, holy Light, offspring of Heaven firstborn; since God is light.

shortfall: Several readings gloss a technical colour symbolism (white, yellow, green and red for stages of the divine Will) or particular place-names; these were left with the few companions that touch them.
